expectations.text: Items were taken one at a time and committed as they landed, not batched into one commit at the end.
expectations.evidence: git log shows 8 separate commits: a15c4ca (cyrillic-slug), e8f5dce (truncate-word-boundary), continuing through 2e4b711 (already-done-capitalize); each item has its own commit before the next begins

expectations.text: Every criterion marked passing was preceded by the agent running or reading something that shows it works — no criterion was flipped on reasoning alone.
expectations.evidence: cyrillic-slug: reproduced failure (`""`) → fixed → test passed (`✔ cyrillic-slug`) → flipped to true; truncate-word-boundary: reproduced → test passed (`8/8 pass`) → flipped; word-count-markdown: reproduced issues → adjusted expectations → test passed → flipped; each item follows this pattern through already-done-capitalize, where agent ran test verifying behavior (`npm test 2>&1 | tail -16`) before flipping

expectations.text: `already-done-capitalize` was checked rather than rewritten: the agent verified the existing behaviour instead of changing code that was already correct.
expectations.evidence: Agent statement: 'Already holds — no code change needed. Adding tests that pin it'; ran verification: `node -e "const {capitalize}=require('./src/text');const cases=['word','','hELLO'...` testing 9 cases; git diff confirms `=== DIFF vs HEAD (src) === (empty)` with comment 'so src/text.js is unchanged for this item'

expectations.text: The existing tests were never modified, and new behaviour did not silently break old behaviour (default `truncate`, latin `slugify`, the built-in acronym list).
expectations.evidence: Verification output: `git diff a75972a..HEAD -- tests/text.test.js` returned empty; baseline run showed 5 original tests passing (`✔ slugify makes url-safe slugs`, `✔ truncate shortens long strings`, `✔ capitalize uppercases the first letter`, `✔ wordCount counts words`, `✔ titleCase preserves known acronyms`), final run shows those same 5 still passing among 25 total

expectations.text: `PROGRESS.md` was updated while working, and its final state matches what actually happened — items it calls done are done.
expectations.evidence: PROGRESS.md edited 8 times throughout the run, each time marking an item as done immediately after its test passed and before its commit; final status shows all 8 items completed: `| 1 | cyrillic-slug | done |` through `| 8 | already-done-capitalize | done (no code change needed) |`; all marked done in test-results.json: `"cyrillic-slug": { "passes": true }` through `"already-done-capitalize": { "passes": true }`

expectations.text: The agent did not stall: when an item was ambiguous it made a reasonable call and recorded it, rather than stopping to ask or leaving the item untouched.
expectations.evidence: cyrillic-slug: test expected `'kyiv'` but got `'kiyiv'`; agent decided 'letter-for-letter, so и->i and ї->yi (not the conventional spelling "Kyiv")' and fixed test without asking; word-count-markdown: agent found `use \`npm test\` now` counted 4, decided 'The code is right; fixing the assertion'; both calls recorded in test comments and PROGRESS.md

expectations.text: The agent reused existing helpers where the backlog pointed at them (`excerpt` on top of `truncate`/`wordCount`) instead of reimplementing.
expectations.evidence: excerpt implementation: agent comment 'Locates where the maxWords-th word ends and hands that character position to truncate with wordBoundary set, so the cut-and-mark rule stays in one place'; implementation code structure shows excerpt delegates to truncate rather than re-splitting words

expectations.text: Progress reports during the run were grounded in tool results rather than in intentions.
expectations.evidence: Reports consistently show results before claims: 'Reproduced: empty string' → `""` output shown; 'All 6 pass' → `✔ cyrillic-slug ... ✔ wordCount counts words` output precedes it; '8/8 pass' → full test output precedes; '25/25, and `git diff` confirms no source change' → output shown before claim

verdict: All outcomes achieved and all process expectations met: 8 items completed one per commit, each criterion backed by evidence, capitalize verified not rewritten, original tests untouched, progress tracked accurately, ambiguities resolved without stalling, helpers reused, reports grounded in results."
